unit.title: Introduction to Electrical Energy and DC Circuits

title: Electrical energy sources — ideal and practical voltage/current sources
summary: Energy-source classification; independent voltage and current sources; ideal and practical source models; source symbols and V–I/I–V characteristics.
transcription_policy: Notebook wording is preserved as written as far as it is safely readable. User-confirmed readings are used where the handwriting was ambiguous; line wrapping is normalized for the web.

pages.heading: Energy sources and ideal voltage source

blocks.text: Energy sources
Independent → voltage source → Ideal, Practical
Independent → current source → Ideal, Practical
Dependent → VCCS, CCCS, CCVS, VCVS

blocks.alt: Notebook-style classification tree of energy sources into independent voltage/current sources with ideal and practical forms, and dependent VCCS, CCCS, CCVS and VCVS sources.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Classification of energy sources

blocks.text: Independent voltage source
Symbol: \(V_s\) / \(V\); a source may also be written as \(V(t)\).

blocks.alt: Notebook-style symbols for DC voltage sources using a cell and a circular source with plus/minus polarity, plus the circular sine-wave symbol for an AC source.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · DC and AC voltage-source symbols

blocks.text: An independent voltage source maintains a voltage (fixed or varying with time) which is not affected by any other quantity.
Ideal voltage source
A two-terminal element in which \(V_s\) is completely independent of current \(I_s\) through its terminals.
In the V–I characteristic, at any time the value of \(V_s\) is constant with respect to current \(I_s\).

blocks.alt: Notebook-style ideal voltage-source two-terminal element with source voltage V_s, current I_s and terminal-voltage label V, alongside a constant-voltage V–I characteristic.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Ideal voltage source and V–I characteristic

pages.heading: Practical voltage source and ideal current-source symbols

blocks.text: Practical voltage source
\[V=V_s-IR\]
Practical voltage source can be considered as series-combination of an ideal voltage source and resistance which is known as source resistance.
The reduction in voltage across the terminals with increasing load current is due to voltage drop in source resistance.
When the value of source resistance is 0, ideal condition is achieved in the voltage source. Hence source resistance/internal resistance of an ideal voltage source is 0.

blocks.alt: Notebook-style practical voltage source shown as source V_s in series with internal resistance R, together with its downward-sloping V–I characteristic and relation V equals V_s minus IR.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Practical voltage source and V–I characteristic

blocks.text: Ideal current source
The source current may be written as a fixed value \(I_1\) or a time-varying value \(I(t)\); the arrow shows the chosen source-current direction.

blocks.alt: Notebook-style strip of three equivalent ideal current-source representations, labelled I_1 or I(t), with arrows showing current direction and a brace marked SAME.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Ideal current-source symbols

blocks.text: Ideal current source
An ideal current source is a two-terminal element in which current \(I_s\) is completely independent of voltage \(V_s\) across its terminals.
If we observe the V–I characteristics of an ideal current source, at any time the value of current \(I_s\) is constant with respect to the voltage across it.

blocks.alt: Notebook-style ideal current source with source current I_s and terminal voltage V, alongside a graph of constant I_s versus output voltage V_o.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Ideal current source and I–V characteristic

blocks.text: Practical current source
\[I=I_s-\dfrac{V}{R}\]
The reduction in current delivered by source is due to current drawn by parallel source resistance.
Ideal condition: \(R=\infty\) (source resistance). Hence source resistance/internal resistance of an ideal current source is \(\infty\).

blocks.alt: Notebook-style practical current-source circuit with ideal source I_s in parallel with source resistance R_s, alongside an I–V characteristic showing practical current decreasing as output voltage V_o increases.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Practical current source and I–V characteristic
